resources.string: Optimizes notification icons on ColorOS and makes them follow the native notification icon specification by fankes@github

When an app is enabled, its colored notification icons are replaced with the monochrome icons provided in the list.\nThe Override option ignores the app\'s own monochrome icon and always uses the one provided in the list.
Keep this off unless needed. Turn it on only when the module is malfunctioning, then send the debug log to the developer so the problem can be located quickly.
While Developer Options is on, the system posts a warning notification after every reboot. When enabled, this nagging notification is removed entirely.
The system posts a notification whenever charging completes, and sometimes it is not even silent. When enabled, this nagging notification is removed entirely.
The system posts a notification whenever Do Not Disturb is turned on, however long it lasts. When enabled, this nagging notification is removed entirely.
Enable compatibility mode if the module detects the notification icon color incorrectly. It is generally not recommended. If any problem occurs, turn it off.

On any version, when enabled, the notification icons in the notification shade use the Material 3 design introduced in Android 12, which adds an outer outline to the icons.\nOn Android 12 and above, the system theme color is used for tinting automatically.
Drag the slider to adjust the corner radius of the icon border in the notification shade.

This option is off by default. When enabled, the notification icons in the notification shade ignore their own tint attribute and are all tinted with the system default color (the uniform color provided by the system). This overrides native notification icon behavior and is only provided for users who need it. We do not recommend enabling it, so please decide based on your own preference.

This option is off by default. When enabled, the notification icons in the notification shade are replaced by the app\'s own icon, while the icons in the status bar are not changed. This overrides native notification icon behavior and is only provided for users who need it. We do not recommend enabling it, so please decide based on your own preference.
ColorOS collapses media notifications by default while playing. When enabled, the notification expands automatically whenever a media notification is posted or playback resumes.
After this is enabled, you can drag the slider to adjust the opacity of the notification shade background. 0% is fully transparent and 100% is opaque.

This is an experimental function that may not be maintained in the future, and has only been tested on ColorOS 12.1 and 13. It cannot be guaranteed to work on every system version or alongside other notification shade theme modules. If there is a conflict, turn this function off or disable the theme module that provides the same function.

Known issues:
(1) Heads-up notifications also become transparent, and at low opacity there is a shadow glow when pulling down the shade, which goes away after releasing. This will be handled later if there is demand.
(2) After collapsed notifications are dismissed automatically (but not completely), the notification background may be fully transparent. This is a system bug, and there is currently no reliable way to tell whether a child layout has been removed from the stacked notification items.
(3) On systems older than ColorOS 12.1, opacity may not take effect on media notifications. Older versions are no longer supported and this will not be fixed.
This option is off by default. When an unadapted colored notification icon is found, the status bar shows a built-in placeholder icon instead, and the icon in the notification shade stays unchanged.

This option is on by default. When the notification icon optimization list contains data, newly installed apps are checked for adaptation data automatically, and you are notified if there is none. If you know that the notification icons of the apps you install follow the native monochrome specification, you can turn this reminder off.
This option is on by default. You can choose the time of day at which the notification icon resources are updated automatically. The module does not need to run in the background.
Hiding the module icon may close this screen, and the module will no longer appear on the launcher. You can still find the module in your Xposed manager and open its settings from there.
In LSPosed, make sure \"Force apps to show launcher icons\" is turned off.
Q. How was this module born?

A. ColorOS, the second-largest system after MIUI, supports native notification icons, but it does not handle the colorful icons pushed by third-party apps, and even the system\'s own icons are colored, which is extremely unfriendly. Moreover, starting with ColorOS 12 the native icons lost their tint attribute, which also undermines the native Android ecosystem.

A. LSPosed is recommended. In its scope, just check \"System UI\". After applying the settings, System UI needs to be restarted. If you installed the \"modern\" variant of the module, on LSPosed 2.1.0+ the module supports hot reload, so later module updates no longer require restarting System UI.
Q. What are the known issues?

A. Known issues:
(1) Due to limited devices, only ColorOS 12, 12.1 and 13 have been tested and confirmed to work. ColorOS 11 issues are debugged and fixed remotely based on feedback from Coolapk users. Other versions are untested, so please try them yourself.
(2) OxygenOS is only supported on versions 12, 12.1 and 13. Other skins based on ColorOS should work in theory. Please test them yourself.
(3) Dynamic System UI refresh is experimental. If the system dark mode changes dynamically, or the resolution or font size is adjusted, the notification icons in the status bar and notification shade may revert or stop working, or black and white block icons may appear during the refresh. In that case, simply restart System UI manually once.
(4) On some devices running ColorOS 12 and 12.1, black and white block icons occasionally appear in the notification shade. This is caused by the system forcibly resetting the icons and cannot be fixed. On devices that support it, updating to ColorOS 13 is recommended. This will not be fixed.
(5) Because ColorOS 15 changed how system notification icons behave and forcibly replaces icons with the colored app icon during icon initialization, the "System Framework" scope was added. If this scope is not checked automatically after installing the module, check it manually and reboot to fix this breakage. Systems older than ColorOS 15 do not need it.
